title: ZORA
summary: Provides opinionated React Native and React Native Web UI components, theme primitives, registries, and reader surfaces built on @ankhorage/surface.
purpose: Give independently released applications a reusable, cross-platform presentation layer with explicit public entrypoints for components, themes, registries, readers, and authoring controls.
responsibilities: Publish React Native and React Native Web UI components and their public props through explicit package entrypoints.
Provide theme primitives, component registries, reader surfaces, and selected feature-specific UI entrypoints.
Compose UI behavior on the published @ankhorage/surface foundation and declared React Native peer dependencies.
boundaries: Does not own application-specific business workflows, persistence, deployment, authentication providers, or infrastructure operations.
Does not execute capabilities or replace the runtime that interprets application descriptors.
Does not require consumers to use an Ankhorage application, repository, or unpublished sibling source.
audience: React Native and React Native Web application authors who need reusable Ankhorage UI components.
Maintainers integrating published ZORA components, themes, registries, readers, or authoring controls into independent applications.
useCases: Render reusable controls, layouts, cards, navigation-adjacent UI, data displays, and specialized feature surfaces in a React Native or web application.
Register and resolve ZORA components for descriptor-driven presentation.
Apply ZORA themes and reader or authoring UI through the package's public entrypoints.

architecture.role: Reusable cross-platform UI and design-system library with feature-owned components and explicit public package subpaths.
invariants: Consumers use published package entrypoints and declared dependencies rather than sibling source imports.
React, React Native, and platform-specific integration remain declared peer or package dependencies at the UI boundary.
Application workflows and provider-specific side effects remain outside the component library.

limitations: Consumers must provide the declared React Native peer dependencies required by the entrypoints they use.
Platform-native behavior is available only where the underlying declared React Native or Expo dependency supports it.
